title: Pipe-select input grammar (SELECT mode, pick_pipe, pipe_selected signal) has zero test coverage
evidence:
scripts/input_router.gd:
	_picked_pipe = flow_view.pick_pipe(screen_pos, camera)
	_mode = Mode.SELECT if _picked_pipe >= 0 else Mode.ORBIT
...
	if was == Mode.SELECT and _picked_pipe >= 0 \
			and screen_pos.distance_to(_press_pos) <= CLICK_SLOP_PX:
		pipe_selected.emit(_picked_pipe)

tests/test_input.gd (the ONLY input coverage, never reaches the pipe branch — grep for pick_pipe|SELECT|pipe_selected|_picked_pipe across tests/ returns nothing):
	check(InputRouter.classify(site) == InputRouter.Mode.DRAW, "press on a node = DRAW")
	check(InputRouter.classify(body) == InputRouter.Mode.ORBIT, "press on the planet body = ORBIT")
	check(InputRouter.classify(null) == InputRouter.Mode.ORBIT, "press on the sky = ORBIT")
detail: The E2.3 story's pipe-select verb (the only player path to QoS; a documented README control) is untested at every level: pick geometry, occlusion guard, click slop, drag-to-orbit fallback, signal wiring, panel open. Even the capture runner bypasses it (calls main._on_pipe_selected directly).
recommended_fix: Add a test_gesture leg: draw a pipe, unproject a path-sample midpoint, press+release cleanly, assert router Mode.SELECT and panel visible; press+drag past slop asserts it becomes orbit.

title: QoS panel command-construction logic (_on_rung lane fallback, _on_apply emission) untested
evidence:
scripts/qos_panel.gd:
func _on_rung(count: int) -> void:
	_alloc = SimBalance.LADDER[count].duplicate()
	# classes on newly-inactive lanes fall back to the highest active lane
	for cls in _cls_lane:
		if _alloc[int(_cls_lane[cls])] <= 0:
...
func _on_apply() -> void:
	if _pipe_id < 0:
		return
	apply_requested.emit(_pipe_id, _alloc.duplicate(), _cls_lane.duplicate())

tests/test_view_purity.gd (the only panel exercise — un-asserted view noise):
			qos.open(2, main.sim)
			qos._on_class_cycle("email")
			qos._on_class_cycle("email")
			qos._on_class_cycle("streaming")
			qos.close_panel()
detail: P2 gap: no test presses a rung or Apply. If the fallback emits a class onto an inactive lane, SimCore silently rejects the whole set_lanes as a no-op — the player's Apply would appear broken with no failing test.
recommended_fix: Headless panel test: open on a real pipe, click rungs, assert _alloc/_cls_lane fallback mapping and that apply_requested emits a valid command that SimCore actually applies (alloc changes).

title: Command-bus invalid-command guards claimed as deterministic no-ops but only 2 of ~6 branches tested
evidence:
scripts/sim/sim_core.gd:
## ... Invalid commands are recorded and
## ignored (deterministic no-ops) — the panel never sends one.
...
	if a < 0 or b < 0 or a >= node_kind.size() or b >= node_kind.size() or a == b:
		return
...
	var p = pipes.get(int(cmd.pipe))
	if p == null:
		return

tests only cover two guards (tests/test_sim_qos.gd):
	check(p.alloc[0] == before[0] and p.alloc[1] == before[1], "invalid ladder (sum > 100) is rejected as a no-op")
	check(int(p.cls_lane.email) == 2, "class cannot be assigned to an inactive lane (rejected)")
detail: P3 error-path blind spot: add_pipe with out-of-range/self node ids, set_lanes on an unknown pipe id, wrong alloc size, and missing keys are happy-path-only; every test add_pipe uses valid indices.
recommended_fix: Extend test_sim_qos._set_lanes_command with no-op legs: add_pipe a==b / a>=N leaves pipes empty; set_lanes on unknown pipe id and alloc.size()!=2/3 leave state + hash behavior pinned.

evidence:

grep for hud|set_breaches|_breach_lines across tests/ returns nothing (only scripts/main.gd:26,71 hits).

title: Loss-latch stickiness (no-chatter) unpinned while the latency twin is pinned
evidence:
tests/test_sim_sla.gd (latency has an explicit stickiness leg):
	var latched_at := int(s.lat_tick)
	drive(sim, 600)
	check(int(sim.sla["email"].lat_tick) == latched_at and bool(sim.sla["email"].lat_breach),
		"SLA: breach latch is sticky-Enter (no chatter)")
(loss is asserted set once, never re-checked after further ticks):
	check(bool(sim.sla["email"].loss_breach), "SLA: email loss breach detected (>30%)")
	check(bool(sim.sla["streaming"].loss_breach), "SLA: streaming loss breach detected (>10%)")
detail: P3: the sticky-Enter doctrine ('ratios dilute, latches must not chatter') applies to both latches; only loss-breach-set is tested, not loss_tick stability across continued overload.
recommended_fix: In _loss_breach_attributable, capture loss_tick, drive 600 more saturated ticks, assert loss_tick unchanged and loss_breach still true for both classes.
